A1.justification: While this specification represents a reasonable compromise, I would only support implementation with robust safeguards in place – particularly regarding data privacy and ongoing monitoring for bias. The inclusion of any sensitive data, even with fairness considerations, feels ethically fraught and requires constant vigilance. Furthermore, clear opt-out mechanisms and transparent communication are essential. I also believe regular student representation on an oversight board is vital to ensure this system truly serves the needs of all learners.

A2.justification: While I appreciate the compromises reflected in this specification, particularly regarding sensitive data and explainability, I remain concerned about relying on predictive modelling at all. My support is contingent upon robust ongoing monitoring of fairness metrics, transparent communication with students, a readily accessible opt-out mechanism, *and* significant investment in preventative, universal support services to address root causes rather than solely identifying ‘at-risk’ individuals. Without these safeguards, I believe the risks outweigh the benefits.

A3.justification: While I appreciate the compromise reflected in this specification, and believe it addresses many ethical concerns raised during the workshop, my support is conditional. The emphasis on limiting sensitive data use is positive, but continuous vigilance against bias remains paramount.
